query: Which clinical factors best explain longer visit durations?

per_column.name: clinical_complexity_score
per_column.rationale: A candidate clinical cause of longer visits; can act as the treatment being attributed. It is not itself a common cause set up alongside a distinct treatment, so it functions as a candidate cause of the outcome.

per_column.name: procedure_needed
per_column.rationale: Whether a procedure is required plausibly increases visit duration directly; it is a candidate cause (treatment), not a common cause adjusted for another treatment.

per_column.name: medication_adjustment
per_column.rationale: A clinical action that lengthens the visit; another candidate cause of the outcome rather than a confounder of a separate treatment.

per_column.name: clinical_detail_level
per_column.rationale: The recorded level of clinical detail is plausibly a consequence of both complexity and visit length (more time/more complexity yields more documentation), so it is downstream, not a common cause; adjusting for it would be a mistake.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply several plausible candidate causes (treatments) of visit duration -- complexity, procedure need, medication adjustment -- so requirement (a) is met. However, requirement (b) is NOT satisfied: none of the columns are genuine confounders, i.e., variables that cause BOTH one of these treatments AND the outcome and must be adjusted to de-bias the attribution. The columns are a bundle of parallel candidate causes with no common-cause adjustment set; a true confounder would be something like patient comorbidity burden, provider/staffing level, or clinic time-of-day load that drives both whether a procedure/complexity occurs and how long the visit runs. clinical_detail_level is downstream (collider/consequence), not a confounder. Because the system surfaced zero real, non-query-named confounders, the causal-attribution capability under test is not demonstrated.
